title: METI: Existential Threat? Probably Yes
summary: Josh and Chuck explain METI (Messaging to Extraterrestrial Intelligence, also called active SETI), the proactive effort to send deliberate signals to alien civilizations rather than only listening. They cover the Great Silence and Fermi paradox, the barn door argument, early proposals (Gauss's wheat fields, Lilienthal-style trench fires), the 1962 Soviet Crimea broadcast, the 1974 Arecibo Message with Frank Drake and Carl Sagan, later attempts (Zeitsev, NASA's Beatles broadcast, Dorito's ad, Joe Davis), Douglas Vakoch and the METI International group, the 2017 transmission to GJ 273b, the Beacon in the Galaxy project, criticisms (unauthorized diplomacy, Declaration of Principles, John Gertz, dark forest theory, existential risk, precautionary principle), and METI's counterarguments. Ends with a listener mail about stall speed correction.

entities.name: Declaration of Principles for Activities Following the Detection of Extraterrestrial Intelligence

segments.title: Opening banter and plug for Inner Cosmos
segments.summary: Hosts banter, plug the new iHeart show Inner Cosmos, and connect the episode to earlier SETI, alien contact, and Golden Records episodes.

segments.title: What METI is and the Great Silence
segments.summary: METI (active SETI) is defined as proactively transmitting signals rather than passively listening. The Great Silence and Fermi paradox are introduced, with Jill Tarter's response, the barn door argument, and the precautionary principle.

segments.title: Early historical proposals and the 1962 Soviet broadcast
segments.summary: Early ideas include Gauss's wheat-field triangles and Lilienthal's burning trenches. The first likely METI broadcast was a Soviet Crimea radar station's Morse code message in November 1962.

segments.title: Arecibo Message and the Golden Records
segments.summary: Frank Drake and Carl Sagan's 1974 Arecibo Message used binary code aimed at M13. The hosts note binary as a possible universal language, and mention Voyager's Golden Records (1977).

segments.title: Later solo broadcasts: Zaitsev, NASA, Dorito's, Joe Davis
segments.summary: Survey of later attempts: Alexander Zaitsev's broadcasts, NASA's Beatles song toward Polaris, Dorito's thirty-second ad sent for six hours, and Joe Davis's artistic transmissions in 1985 and 2009.

segments.title: METI International and the 2017 transmission
segments.summary: Douglas Vakoch left SETI to found METI International after SETI refused to pursue messaging. The group's 2017 transmission included math, music, and a clock.

segments.title: Beacon in the Galaxy and Goldilocks zone targets
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the 2017 message's target GJ 273b (about twelve light years away), and the JPL Beacon in the Galaxy project. Better exoplanet detection and roughly twenty Goldilocks-zone candidate planets make directed messages more feasible.

segments.title: Criticisms: unauthorized diplomacy and risk
segments.summary: Critics such as John Gertz call METI unauthorized diplomacy, citing the Declaration of Principles. Frank Drake was criticized after Arecibo. Critics argue international regulation is needed. Breakthrough Listen is cited as a reason to keep listening first.

segments.title: METI counterarguments and the I Love Lucy broadcast
segments.summary: Proponents argue advanced civilizations may be waiting for a signal, and that Earth has already leaked TV signals such as I Love Lucy. The hosts say the leakage argument is weak because the signals are degraded and hard to detect at distance.

segments.title: Dark forest theory and existential risk
segments.summary: The dark forest theory suggests quiet survival. Critics worry about hostile aliens, while the hosts note the debate is about uncertainty, not certainty of hostility, and point out that alien contact has had catastrophic outcomes on Earth.

segments.title: Closing remarks on alien contact
segments.summary: Light closing banter about alien movie plots and the end of the alien contact series, including UFO episodes.

segments.title: Listener mail: stall speed correction
segments.summary: Listener TJ corrects an earlier skydiving episode claim: stall speed refers to wing lift loss, not engine stall.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank listeners and give the email address; show credits follow.
